about.title: Morgan Hill Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Morgan Hill residents rely on a mix of local clinics and larger Santa Clara County medical centers for care, and most of the time that care goes as expected. But when a surgical error, missed diagnosis, medication mistake, or birth injury causes real harm, patients and families are often left confused about whether what happened was simply an unfortunate outcome or something more. California law sets a high bar for these claims — a qualified medical expert almost always has to review the case, and strict notice and filing deadlines apply. LawProactive doesn't practice law or make that determination for you. Instead, we connect Morgan Hill patients and families with an independent attorney in our network who can review medical records, evaluate whether the standard of care was met, and explain what options may exist. There's no fee to get connected, and the attorneys work on contingency, meaning they're paid only if you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before MICRA Deadlines Pass

items.title: Short, Strict Deadlines
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice claims to be filed within one year of discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself. Waiting to explore your options can mean losing them entirely.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed in California, the healthcare provider must typically receive written notice at least 90 days in advance. An attorney can help make sure this step is handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: Because a bad outcome alone isn't proof of malpractice, California cases generally require a qualified medical expert to evaluate whether the standard of care was actually violated. An independent attorney can help arrange that kind of review.

items.question: Does a bad medical outcome automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that medicine involves risk, and a poor result on its own isn't enough to prove malpractice. There generally has to be evidence that a provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care, which is why an expert review is usually required.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but never more than three years from the date of the injury itself. There's also a 90-day pre-suit notice requirement that has to happen before a lawsuit is filed, so it's worth talking to someone sooner rather than later.

items.question: I live in Morgan Hill but was treated at a facility outside the city — does that matter?
items.answer: Not necessarily. What matters most is where the care was provided and where the harm occurred, not simply your home address. An independent attorney can look at the specifics of your situation, including which facility and providers were involved, regardless of whether that's in Morgan Hill or elsewhere in Santa Clara County.
